rows.text: During this frantic and riotous career several thought of attempting his life. But when one or two conspiracies had been detected and the rest were waiting for a favourable opportunity, two men made   common cause and succeeded, with the connivance of his most influential freedmen and the officers of the praetorian guard; for although the charge that these last were privy to one of the former conspiracies was false, they realised that Caligula hated and feared them. rows.text: One may form an idea of the state of those times from the following facts. For not even when the murder was made known was it at once believed, but it was suspected that Gaius himself had made up and circulated the report of his assassination, to find out by that means what men thought of him. The conspirators too had not agreed on a successor for the empire; and the senate was so unanimous in asserting its liberty, that the consuls called the first meeting, not in the senate house, because it was named the Julian, but on the Capitol; while some in expressing their opinions proposed that the memory of the Caesars be wiped out and their temples destroyed. It was further observed and noted as a special circumstance that all the Caesars who bore the forename Gaius perished by the sword, beginning with the one who was slain in the times of Cinna.
